references: [[http://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/7740877][Brubaker et al., IEEE Trans. Pattern Anal. Mach. Intell., 2017]]
form.help:
Apply non-uniform refinement to achieve higher resolution and map
    quality, especially for membrane proteins. Non-uniform refinement
    iteratively accounts for regions of a structure that have disordered or
    flexible density causing local loss of resolution. Accounting for these
    regions and dynamically estimating their locations can significantly
    improve resolution in other regions as well as overall map quality by
    impacting the alignment of particles and reducing the tendency for
    refinement algorithms to over-fit disordered regions.

params.name: runName
params.label: Run name:
params.help: Select run name label to identify this run.

params.name: _objComment
params.label: Comment
params.help: Protocol comments

params.name: _useQueue
params.label: Use a queue engine?
params.help:
Click Yes if you want to send this execution to a queue engine like Slurm, Torque, ...
    The queue commands to launch and stop jobs should be configured at
    _/home/yunior/Yunior/Projects/ScipionWeb/ScipionAPI/scipion_home/config/hosts.conf_ file.
    
    See https://scipion-em.github.io/docs/release-3.0.0/docs/scipion-modes/host-configuration.html for more information.

params.name: _prerequisites
params.label: Wait for
params.help:
Specify a comma separated list of protocol IDs if you want
    to *schedule* this protocol and wait for those protocols to finish before
    starting this one.
    
    This function will allow you to "schedule" many
    runs that will be executed after each other.
     
    See https://scipion-em.github.io/docs/release-3.0.0/docs/user/scipion-gui.html#waiting-for-other-protocols for more information.

params.name: gpuList
params.label: GPU IDs
params.help: This argument is necessary. By default, the protocol will attempt to launch on GPU 0. You can override the default allocation by providing a list of which GPUs (0,1,2,3, etc) to use. GPU are separated by ",". For example: "0,1,5"

params.name: inputParticles
params.label: Input particles
params.help: Select the input images from the project.

params.name: referenceVolume
params.label: Input volume
params.help: Initial reference 3D map, it should have the same dimensions and the same pixel size as your input particles.

params.name: refMask
params.label: Mask to be applied to this map(Optional)
params.help: A volume mask containing a (soft) mask with the same dimensions as the reference(s), and values between 0 and 1, with 1 being 100% protein and 0 being 100% solvent. The reconstructed reference map will be multiplied by this mask. If no mask is given, a soft spherical mask based on the <radius> of the mask for the experimental images will be applied.

params.name: symmetryGroup
params.label: Symmetry
params.help:
Symmetry as defined by cryosparc. Please note that Dihedral symmetry in cryosparc is defined with respectto y axis (Dyn).
If no symmetry is present, use C1.
Symmetry String (C, D, I, O, T). E.g. C1, D7, C4, etc

params.name: symmetryOrder
params.label: Symmetry Order
params.help: Order of symmetry.

params.name: refine_symmetry_do_align
params.label: Do symmetry alignment
params.help: Align the input structure to the symmetry axes

params.name: refine_do_init_scale_est
params.label: Re-estimate greyscale level of input reference

params.name: refine_num_final_iterations
params.label: Number of extra final passes
params.help: Number of extra passes through the data to do after the GS-FSC resolution has stopped improving

params.name: refine_res_init
params.label: Initial lowpass resolution (A)
params.help: Applied to input structure

params.name: refine_res_gsfsc_split
params.label: GSFSC split resolution (A)
params.help: Resolution beyond which two GS-FSC halves are independent

params.name: refine_clip
params.label: Enforce non-negativity
params.help: Clip negative density. Probably should be false

params.name: refine_window
params.label: Skip interpolant premult
params.help: Softly window the structure in real space with a spherical window. Should be true

params.name: refine_skip_premult
params.label: Window structure in real space
params.help: Leave this as true

params.name: refine_ignore_dc
params.label: Ignore DC component
params.help: Ignore the DC component of images. Should be true

params.name: refine_batchsize_init
params.label: Initial batchsize
params.help: Number of images used in the initial iteration. Set to zero to autotune

params.name: refine_batchsize_epsilon
params.label: Batchsize epsilon
params.help: Controls batch size when autotuning batchsizes. Set closer to zero for larger batches

params.name: refine_batchsize_snrfactor
params.label: Batchsize snrfactor
params.help: Specifies the desired improvement in SNR from the images when autotuning batchsizes. Directly multiplies the number of images in the batch

params.name: refine_scale_start_iter
params.label: Scale min/use start iter
params.help: Iteration to start minimizing over per-particle scale

params.name: refine_noise_model
params.label: Noise model:
params.help: Noise model to be used. Valid options are white, coloured or symmetric. Symmetric is the default, meaning coloured with radial symmetry

params.name: refine_noise_priorw
params.label: Noise priorw
params.help: Weight of the prior for estimating noise (units of # of images)

params.name: refine_noise_initw
params.label: Noise initw
params.help: Weight of the initial noise estimate (units of # of images)

params.name: refine_noise_init_sigmascale
params.label: Noise initial sigma-scale
params.help: Scale factor initially applied to the base noise estimate

params.name: refine_mask
params.label: Mask:
params.help: Type of masking to use. Either "dynamic", "static", or "null"

params.name: refine_dynamic_mask_thresh_factor
params.label: Dynamic mask threshold (0-1)
params.help: Level set threshold for selecting regions that are included in the dynamic mask. Probably don't need to change this

params.name: refine_dynamic_mask_near_ang
params.label: Dynamic mask near (A)
params.help: Controls extent to which mask is expanded. At the near distance, the mask value is 1.0 (in A)

params.name: refine_dynamic_mask_far_ang
params.label: Dynamic mask far (A)
params.help: Controls extent to which mask is expanded. At the far distance the mask value becomes 0.0 (in A)

params.name: refine_dynamic_mask_start_res
params.label: Dynamic mask start resolution (A)
params.help: Map resolution at which to start dynamic masking (in A)

params.name: refine_dynamic_mask_use_abs
params.label: Dynamic mask use absolute value
params.help: Include negative regions if they are more negative than the threshold

params.name: refine_compute_batch_size
params.label: GPU batch size of images
params.help: Batch size of images to process at a time on the GPU. If you run out of GPU memory, try setting this to a small number to override the auto-detect procedure.

params.name: refine_defocus_refine
params.label: Optimize per-particle defocus
params.help: Minimize over per-particle defocus at each iteration of refinement. The optimal defocus will be used for backprojection as well, and will be written out at each iteration. Defocus refinement will start only once refinement with current defocus values converges. Beware that with small/disordered proteins, defocus refinement may actually make resolutions worse.

params.name: crl_num_plots
params.label: Num. particles to plot
params.help: Number of particles to make plots for. After this many, stop plotting to save time.

params.name: crl_min_res_A
params.label: Minimum Fit Res (A)
params.help: The minimum resolution to use during refinement of image aberrations.

params.name: crl_df_range
params.label: Defocus Search Range (A +/-)
params.help: Defocus search range in Angstroms, searching both above and below the input defocus by this amount

params.name: refine_ctf_global_refine
params.label: Optimize per-group CTF params
params.help: Optimize the per-exposure-group CTF parameters (for higher-order aberrations) at each iteration of refinement. The optimal CTF will be used for backprojection as well, and will be written out at each iteration. CTF refinement will start only once refinement with current CTF values converges. Beware that with small/disordered proteins, CTF refinement may actually make resolutions worse.

params.name: crg_num_plots
params.label: Num. groups to plot
params.help: Number of exposure groups to make plots for. After this many, stop plotting to save time.

params.name: crg_min_res_A
params.label: Minimum Fit Res (A)
params.help: The minimum resolution to use during refinement of image aberrations.

params.name: crg_do_tilt
params.label: Fit Tilt
params.help: Whether to fit beam tilt.

params.name: crg_do_trefoil
params.label: Fit Trefoil
params.help: Whether to fit beam trefoil.

params.name: crg_do_spherical
params.label: Fit Spherical Aberration
params.help: Whether to fit spherical aberration.

params.name: crg_do_tetrafoil
params.label: Fit Tetrafoil
params.help: Whether to fit beam tetrafoil.

params.name: refine_do_ews_correct
params.label: Do EWS correction
params.help: Whether or not to correct for the curvature of the Ewald Sphere.

params.name: refine_do_ews_correct_align
params.label: Do EWS correction in alignment
params.help: Whether or not to correct for the curvature of the Ewald Sphere.

params.name: refine_ews_zsign
params.label: EWS curvature sign
params.help: Whether to use positive or negative curvature in Ewald Sphere correction.

params.name: refine_ews_simple
params.label: EWS correction method
params.help: Whether to use the simple insertion method, or to use an iterative optimization method, for Ewald Sphere correction.

params.name: compute_use_ssd
params.label: Cache particle images on SSD
params.help: Whether or not to copy particle images to the local SSD before running. The cache is persistent, so after caching once, particles should be available for subsequent jobs that require the same data. Not using an SSD can dramatically slow down processing.

params.name: compute_lane
params.label: Lane name:
params.help: The scheduler lane name to add the protocol execution

params.name: refine_do_marg
params.label: Adaptive Marginalization
params.help: Efficiently marginalize over poses and shifts using an auto-tuning adaptive sampling strategy. Can improve results on small molecules.

params.name: refine_nu_enable
params.label: Non-uniform refine enable
params.help: Enable cross-validation-optimal non-uniform regularization during refinement.

params.name: refine_nu_filtertype
params.label: Non-uniform filter type
params.help: butterworth, rect, or gaussian

params.name: refine_nu_order
params.label: Non-uniform filter order
params.help: Order of the butterworth filter used for cross-validation-optimal regularization. Default to 8, probably no need to change this.

params.name: refine_nu_awf
params.label: Non-uniform AWF
params.help: Adaptive Window Factor for cross-validation-optimal regularization. Trade off between fast transitions between regions (AWF should be lower) and more accurate local cross-validation test (AWF should be higher). Default of 3 is good, can try as low as 1.5

launch.label: Launch
launch.help: Start the protocol from its current configuration

restart.label: Restart
restart.help: Restart the protocol execution from scratch (keeps current params).
